text: After nearly a year in orbit, Scott Kelly was reported to be about two inches taller.
In microgravity, the spine is unloaded.
It can straighten and lengthen, temporarily increasing an astronaut's height.
NASA says the increase can reach three percent.
It's not a sudden growth spurt in the bones.
Back on Earth, gravity loads the spine again, and astronauts return to their usual height.
It just doesn't let you keep it.
